The best chain on garnet is QB11-QB12-QB7, with QB12 in the middle. I read this from garnet's current default calibration, set f81c45da-6e73-4b5d-a0fe-72c75635fade, whose quality metrics were created at 2026-10-21 16:42Z.

How I picked it:
- The calibration lists 28 CZ pairs, and every pair has an IRB fidelity.
- I checked every chain of 3 connected qubits and multiplied its two CZ fidelities.
- The QB11-QB12 fidelity is 0.998693. The QB12-QB7 fidelity is 0.998016. Their product is 0.996712, which is the highest.
- The runner-up is QB12-QB11-QB16 at 0.994689.

What I ran:
- I ran one 3-qubit GHZ circuit on garnet:mock with 200 shots. The job ID is 01a160a7-127e-7320-baba-983bbbb450d4, and it completed.
- QB12 was rotated into an equal mix of 0 and 1.
- Two CZ gates then copied QB12's value onto QB11 and onto QB7. Each CZ had a quarter-turn rotation on the target qubit before and after it. The CZ gates ran only on the pairs QB12-QB11 and QB12-QB7.
- All 3 qubits were measured.
- I read the circuit back from the server. It has exactly 2 CZ gates and measures QB11, QB12 and QB7.

What the counts show:
- Each bitstring reads in the order QB11, QB12, QB7.
- The counts were 000: 42, 011: 52, 100: 56 and 111: 50.
- A noise-free simulation of this exact circuit gives 000 half the time and 111 half the time.
- The mock does not run the circuit. It returns random bits. That is why it shows 011 and 100, which a real GHZ state would not give.
- The mock run shows that the circuit is valid on those qubits and gates. It does not test the physics.

The principle:
- In a GHZ state, all 3 qubits are linked. Each one reads 0 or 1 at random, but all 3 always give the same answer.
- On real hardware, the share of 000 plus 111 shows how well the entanglement holds up.
- Every CZ gate adds some error. That is why the chain with the highest product of CZ fidelities is the best place to run this circuit.

I spent no real QPU credits.
